extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit grant writers, development staff, and small-organization leaders preparing proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, tactical guidance for drafting competitive grant proposals for nonprofit organizations, emphasizing clear problem statements, funder alignment, measurable outcomes, accurate budgets, and collaborative review. Geared toward improving proposal narrative, tone, and sustainability planning to increase funding success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burying the “Why”
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don’t make the need crystal clear in the first few paragraphs, you’ve lost your reader. Don’t assume funders know why your work matters—tell them upfront and back it up with data and heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a compelling problem statement. Hook them with the urgency, then ease into the details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Like a Robot
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that read like they were written by a committee of beige index cards are bland and get lost; reviewers are human and respond to voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with clarity and warmth. Use real stories and avoid 'jargon soup.' Make your proposal something people want to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overloading on Data, Underloading on Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A flood of statistics that replaces story won’t move a funder—numbers must show the real-world impact behind them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data to reinforce your message, not dominate it. Pair numbers with a compelling narrative so the impact is clear and tangible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignoring the Funder’s Priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: If your project isn’t aligned with the funder’s goals, it’s unlikely to be funded—even if it’s a great project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor your proposal to each funder: reference their mission, mirror their language, and show how your work helps them reach their goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being Vague About Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague promises like 'empower the community' or 'break down a barrier' don’t tell funders what will actually change or how success will be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about what will change, for whom, and how you will measure it. Funders want results they can visualize and evaluate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossing Over the Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong narrative undermined by a mismatched or unrealistic budget (contradictions, wishful thinking, inflated line items) is a red flag; even obvious mistakes like submitting the wrong year’s budget can doom an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your budget matches your activities. Include justifications and a budget narrative that gives a complete picture. It’s acceptable and necessary to budget for admin time; be transparent and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing the Follow-Up Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders want to know what happens after the grant period; if a project appears unable to continue past the final report, funders may consider it unsustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a sustainability or follow-up plan—even a modest one—to show you’re thinking long-term about continuation, scaling, or next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgetting the Human Element
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal focuses only on numbers and not the real people served, you miss your most powerful asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share a respectful, anonymized story of someone your work has helped so funders can see the human impact behind the metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skipping the Proofread
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting proposals with typos, missing attachments, or template placeholders (e.g., 'Dear [Insert Funder Name]') signals carelessness and undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check everything and then have a fresh pair of eyes review the proposal to catch errors, missing materials, and personalization issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trying to Do It All Alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant writing is a team sport; working in isolation can miss key insights, produce weaker applications, and lead to burnout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate with program staff, finance, leadership, and past participants. Involving others strengthens accuracy, authenticity, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate, Stay Curious, and Seek Help
rubrics_metrics.description: No one nails every proposal; strong grant writers stay curious, keep learning, and are willing to tweak their process—even mid-proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt continuous improvement: learn from wins and losses, be open to feedback, and bring in outside help or a second set of eyes when needed.
